# Jeninnet.Localization v1.0.0-preview.3 — Hardening the Contract

`v1.0.0-preview.3` is the third public preview of **Jeninnet.Localization**, a modular
localization framework for .NET. It adds **no new public API**. The release freezes the surface,
turns the project's assumptions into evidence, and ships the same 44-package set with a cleaner
dependency, performance, and supply-chain story.

That is the point of a release candidate: the useful work is no longer "what else can we add?" but
"what have we proved?".

## What the framework gives you

Jeninnet.Localization is built around one deterministic pipeline. A key resolves through exactly
one registered message provider; culture fallback has one owner; formatting and plural rules are
explicit; and the store-backed `IStringLocalizer` bridge lets ASP.NET Core code keep the framework
contract without giving up the pipeline.

The 44 packages cover the complete working surface:

- **Core and contracts** — `Abstractions`, `Core`, `Storage`: providers, localizer, formatters,
  plural and ICU support, fallback, diagnostics, and DI registration.
- **Catalog providers** — Memory, JSON, INI, TOML, XML, ResX, Satellite, PO/MO, Pseudo, SQLite,
  SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and the EF Core resource-set store.
- **Composition** — in-memory and distributed message caches with single-flight coalescing, and an
  ordered composite provider with first-exact-wins semantics.
- **Machine translation** — Azure Translator, DeepL, and Google Translate behind the canonical
  provider contract, with caching, batching, glossaries, translation memory, and resilience where
  the provider supports them.
- **Translator workflow** — CSV, PO, ResX, and XLIFF interchange with shared keys, statuses, and
  notes; plus the vendor-neutral TMS contract and the Crowdin and Weblate connectors.
- **Hosts** — ASP.NET Core request localization, MVC validation and view localization,
  DataAnnotations, Blazor, JavaScript delivery, Avalonia, MAUI, WinUI, and diagnostics/health
  checks.
- **Tooling** — typed key generation from JSON, ResX, PO, and XLIFF; the `JLNLOC001`–`JLNLOC006`
  analyzers and code fixes; and the `jeninnet-localization-keys` parity CLI with SARIF and
  baselines.
- **One discoverability package** — `Jeninnet.Localization` references `Abstractions`, `Core`, and
  `Storage`; the one-provider rule still applies.

Runtime libraries target **.NET 10 (LTS)** and **.NET 11 (STS)** from the same code. The MAUI and
WinUI host integrations stay on their host frameworks. Native AOT is exercised by a published
smoke application, not asserted from a checkbox.

## What changed in preview.3

### The API is frozen

All **44 public-API baselines** are content-identical to the current tree. The only public break in
the preview line remains `ProviderFeature` → `ProviderFeatures`; member names and values are
unchanged. Six deliberate raw-CRUD members remain `[Obsolete]`, and the architecture test allows
exactly those six. A change that alters a public signature is now a reviewed event, not an accident
that slips into a build.

### The support matrix is evidence

The compatibility page records the verified **OS × TFM × AOT × host × database** matrix, including
real SQL Server 2025, MySQL 9, and PostgreSQL 17 runtime lookups. The matrix states what was run and
where; it does not turn "not tested here" into "unsupported forever".

### The hot paths are measured

The performance evidence was regenerated on 2026-11-23 with two runs per runtime and
BenchmarkDotNet short-run passes for the five hot-path classes. It found a real regression: the
preview.3 deduplication refactor had made memory-cache hits pay async state-machine overhead
(86–100 ns instead of the preview.2 range of 60–66 ns). The engine now reads the in-memory store
synchronously and returns a completed `ValueTask`; the post-fix passes measure 68–72 ns, with the
direct lookup unchanged as the control. The distributed backend keeps its asynchronous path.

The page publishes conditions, medians, allocations, and caveats. It does not publish an SLO.

### The supply chain is inspectable

Every release now carries an **SPDX 2.2 SBOM** generated from the packed `.nupkg`/`.snupkg` files
and a GitHub **build-provenance attestation**. The packages are source-linked and hashed. NuGet.org
repository signing, SourceLink, the hashes, the SBOM, and the attestation form the verification
chain. Author certificate signing is deliberately deferred until a certificate and rotation policy
exist; the release notes say so instead of implying otherwise.

### The package set is validated before publication

- 44 `.nupkg` and 42 `.snupkg` files are packed with `EnablePackageValidation=true`.
- A clean consumer solution restores the **packed** packages from a local folder feed, not from
  project references, and runs 11 tests per TFM.
- The dependency graph is checked for prohibited edges; every internal dependency is pinned to the
  same version; package READMEs, `LICENSE`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, and the shared icon travel
  with every package.
- The analyzer, style, and formatting gates are enforced at info severity. The tracked
  analyzer-message ledger is zero.

### Dependency and toolchain currency

SonarAnalyzer 10.37, Windows SDK BuildTools 10.0.28000, and the in-lane Npgsql 10.0.4 patch are
applied. .NET 11 servicing is re-verified with SDK/runtime `11.0.100`/`11.0.0`; Roslyn `5.12`
matches the compiler; Avalonia moves to `12.2.0`. Five major upgrades remain deferred with recorded
exit criteria: Windows App SDK 2.x, MAUI 11, the WebView 11 package, Npgsql 11 on the shared net10
lane, and the test-only Logging.Debug 11. The Windows App SDK 1.8 patch stays at the runner-compatible
pin because a newer pin requires a newer runtime than CI serves.

### Documentation and package pages

The English and Arabic installation, compatibility, release-notes, known-limitations, package-map,
release-checklist, parity, and strongly-typed-key pages are aligned to preview.3. Release status now
points at NuGet and GitHub Releases as the canonical published state, so a preview does not leave a
stale "latest" claim in the README. Package READMEs carry real compatibility sections and pin the
version they ship with.

## Getting started

```powershell
dotnet add package Jeninnet.Localization.Core --version 1.0.0-preview.3
dotnet add package Jeninnet.Localization.Providers.Json --version 1.0.0-preview.3
```

Register the pipeline and exactly one provider:

```csharp
using Jeninnet.Localization.Core.Extensions;
using Jeninnet.Localization.Providers.Json.Extensions;

services.AddLocalization(options => options.DefaultCulture = "en");
services.AddJsonLocalizationProviders(AppContext.BaseDirectory, ["en", "ar"]);
```

The [quick start](https://tareknajem04.github.io/Jeninnet.Localization/en/01-getting-started/03-quick-start.html)
builds a complete two-culture console application, including fallback behavior.

## Upgrading from preview.2

- **Breaking (preview scope):** `ProviderFeature` is now `ProviderFeatures`. Update type references;
  member names and values are unchanged.
- **Additive:** provider options derive from the shared abstract `TranslationProviderOptions`.
  Existing property usage is source-compatible, and configuration binding continues to work.
- **Behavior:** lookup, fallback, formatting, and provider-selection semantics are unchanged. The
  full suite (2139 passed / 1 skipped per TFM with the database services running) is the evidence.
- **Packages:** pin `1.0.0-preview.3`; `1.0.0-preview.2` remains available as the previous preview.

## Verification

- Both solutions build with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- 2139 tests passed / 1 skipped on each of `net10.0` and `net11.0` with SQL Server 2025, MySQL 9,
  and PostgreSQL 17 running; host integrations: 3 passed / 1 skipped.
- API baselines: 44/44 content-identical; `api-compat` acknowledges only the rename.
- Consumer validation: 11/11 per TFM from the packed local feed.
- Native AOT `win-x64`: `SMOKE OK` on both runtimes; Linux AOT runs in CI.
- Docs: docfx metadata and site build with zero warnings; 990 relative links resolve; Arabic text
  checks pass.
- Supply chain: SPDX 2.2 SBOM with 393 packages and 87 files; provenance attestation covers every
  package and symbol package.

## Preview scope and boundaries

`1.0.0-preview.3` is a preview, not a stable `1.0.0`. The surface is complete enough to build,
evaluate, and pilot against, but the project may still adjust it before the stable release. Pin the
exact version, read `CHANGELOG.md` before upgrading, and treat preview packages as evaluation builds
rather than a long-term support commitment.

The release does not hide its boundaries: Windows App SDK, MAUI, and WebView majors are deferred
together with their host lanes; Npgsql 11 waits for a lane decision; macOS AOT is not verified
locally; performance numbers come from one machine and are evidence, not a capacity promise. The
[known limitations](https://tareknajem04.github.io/Jeninnet.Localization/en/03-reference/10-known-limitations.html)
page records each one.
